reason: Researched this week (WebSearch, plus BHF's Q3 2026 10-Q pulled from EDGAR and BHF daily closes from Yahoo). The XLE stop fired on 11-05 at 61.63 (-11.5% realized) and the proceeds sit in 4% cash, so the book is now 22% BHF and 78% cash. The BHF thesis has changed in timing but is not broken. The Q3 10-Q, filed this week, says HSR, FINRA and CFIUS are all done and every condition except Delaware/New York/Massachusetts insurance approval is satisfied or waived. It also says approvals 'are not expected to be received in time' for the Dec 6 Outside Date, and that BHF and Aquarian 'remain committed to the Merger' and are negotiating an extension. So Dec 6 is now an extend-or-walk decision, not a closing date. A signed extension would remove the overhang, and a walk would hit the stop. At $42.60 against $70 cash (~64% gross upside), the market prices a low completion probability. The downside has support: Q3 adjusted EPS was $9.12, RBC 415-435% and holdco liquidity $1.0B; Sixth Street/Talcott bid ~$55 in 2025 and has restated interest as a fallback; and on 11-06 the stock rose 3.6% on roughly 2x normal volume after the extension disclosure. The existing -15% stop (~$38.1) caps the break scenario at about 3.3% of NAV, and 22% remains the right risk-sized weight for a binary outcome. I found no new hard catalyst this week worth paying churn for, and replacing the book to move the stop or resize would cost basis points for no edge. Hold BHF with its stop and TP unchanged, keep the rest in cash, and revisit when an extension or termination is announced. Risk to watch: Aquarian using the extension talks to cut the $70 price. I found no report of that.
